title: Persona ONYX Government Dashboard Source-Code Exposure
summary: Independent security researchers found roughly 2,456 files (53MB) of source code from Persona's FedRAMP-authorized government identity-verification dashboard publicly exposed on a Google Cloud server, revealing facial-recognition watchlist screening, PEP checks, and direct Suspicious Activity Report filing capabilities.
details: On February 19, 2026, a security researcher known as Celeste (vmfunc), working with colleagues MDLcsgo and DziurwaF, discovered that a development configuration path on a FedRAMP-authorized Google Cloud endpoint operated by identity-verification company Persona (app.onyx.withpersona-gov.com) was publicly serving unminified TypeScript source maps. These source maps allowed reconstruction of roughly 2,456 files totalling approximately 53MB of Persona's government-facing 'ONYX' dashboard codebase. The exposed code reportedly revealed 269 distinct verification checks available to government customers, including facial-recognition matching against watchlists, adverse-media screening across 14 categories (including terrorism and espionage), politically-exposed-person (PEP) facial-similarity scoring, biometric data retention policies of up to three years, and functionality to file Suspicious Activity Reports directly to the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and Canada's FINTRAC. The exposure was of source code and system architecture rather than confirmed theft of individual user records. Persona's CEO characterized the exposed material as 'publicly available front-end information' rather than a security vulnerability. Following the disclosure, Discord terminated its use of Persona for UK age-verification trials, and researchers separately noted Persona is also used by OpenAI/ChatGPT for identity verification.

title: Veriff Breach Exposes Total Wireless Customer IDs
summary: An unauthorized party accessed identity-verification vendor Veriff's systems, exposing government ID images and personal details for 8,583 Total Wireless customers who had verified their identity for a promotional offer.
details: Total Wireless, a Verizon-owned prepaid wireless carrier, disclosed to multiple US state attorneys general that an unauthorized party gained access to data stored within the systems of its identity-verification vendor, Veriff, rather than Total Wireless's own network. The breach occurred on November 18, 2025 and was discovered by December 10, 2025. Investigations determined approximately 8,583 Total Wireless customers were affected. Compromised data included images of government-issued identification documents (such as driver's licenses) submitted during the verification process for a promotional offer, along with associated names, mailing addresses, and dates of birth. Class-action lawsuits were subsequently filed alleging Veriff and Total Wireless failed to adequately safeguard personally identifiable information.

title: Police National Legal Database (PNLD) Data Theft
summary: The UK's Police National Legal Database confirmed a data security incident exposing the names, organizations, and work email addresses of police officers, staff, and criminal-justice professionals, with stolen data subsequently published on the dark web.
details: The Police National Legal Database (PNLD), a legal-lookup and reference service relied upon by police forces and criminal justice agencies across the UK, identified a data security incident on July 26, 2026. The organization confirmed that information including the names, organizations, and work email addresses of police officers, police staff, and other criminal justice professionals and government partners had been compromised and subsequently published on the dark web. Cybercriminals claimed to have taken approximately 135,000 pieces of data, in an incident reported alongside a related hack of the UK Department for Education affecting parent and staff contact details. PNLD stated there was no evidence that passwords or other authentication credentials had been compromised, and it was investigating alongside specialist cybersecurity firms and the National Crime Agency.
